question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Madras / Fort St. George — Location]
options: Madras — Located on the Coromandel Coast (southeastern coast of India)
Madras — Situated in present-day Tamil Nadu
Fort St. George — Built on land leased from the Nayaka ruler of the Chandragiri kingdom
Madras — Located on the Malabar Coast (southwestern coast of India)
wrong_fact: Madras is on the Coromandel (southeastern) coast, NOT the Malabar (southwestern) coast. The Malabar coast runs along present-day Kerala.
explanation: Madras (Chennai) lies on the southeastern Coromandel coast of India in present-day Tamil Nadu. The land was leased in 1639 by Francis Day from the Nayaka chieftain of Chandragiri (a successor state of the Vijayanagara Empire). Fort St. George was built there and completed in 1644. The Malabar coast is entirely different — it is the southwestern coast of India in modern Kerala, known for pepper trade with Calicut, Cochin, etc.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Madras / Fort St. George — Key Facts]
options: Fort St. George — First English fort in India, completed around 1644
Francis Day — English factor who negotiated the lease of Madraspatnam in 1639
Andrew Cogan — Francis Day's superior who co-founded the Madras settlement
Fort St. George — Named after the patron saint of Portugal
wrong_fact: Fort St. George is named after Saint George, the patron saint of England, NOT Portugal. Portugal's patron saint is associated with different dedications.
explanation: Saint George is the patron saint of England (also of other countries, but in the Indian colonial context, Fort St. George clearly honours England's patron saint). The fort was built by the English East India Company at Madraspatnam after Francis Day secured the lease in 1639; Andrew Cogan was the senior factor who approved the project. Completed around 1644, it became the first English fort in India and the nucleus of modern Chennai. Attributing the name to Portugal is a deliberate wrong-fact trap.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Madras — Political & Administrative Context]
options: Madras Presidency — Formally established with Fort St. George as its headquarters
Elihu Yale — Served as President of Madras and later donated to Yale University (USA)
Fort St. David — English fort near Cuddalore south of Madras, used as a refuge during Mughal attacks on Surat
Job Charnock — Founded the English settlement at Madras (Madraspatnam) in 1639
wrong_fact: Job Charnock did NOT found Madras. He is credited with founding Calcutta (1690). Madras was founded by Francis Day and Andrew Cogan in 1639.
explanation: Job Charnock is historically associated with the founding of Calcutta — he settled at Sutanuti (near modern Calcutta) in 1690, which eventually became Fort William. Madras was established in 1639 when Francis Day (a factor from the Masulipatnam council) negotiated the lease of Madraspatnam from the Chandragiri Nayaka ruler. Elihu Yale did serve as President of Madras (1687–92) and his later donation to a Connecticut college led it to be renamed Yale University. Fort St. David near Cuddalore was indeed another English outpost on the Coromandel coast.
